problems.title: An exact fraction calculation
problems.question: Evaluate $\dfrac{(83\tfrac5{18}-85\tfrac7{30})\div2\tfrac23}{0.04}\cdot(-3/11)$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Convert mixed numbers and decimals to fractions; divide by multiplying by the reciprocal.
steps: The mixed-number difference is $7495/90-7671/90=-88/45$. Dividing by 8/3 gives −11/15.
Dividing by 1/25 gives −55/3. Multiplying by −3/11 gives 5.

problems.title: Clear denominators in a linear equation
problems.question: Solve $(3x-1)/5-(1-2x)/2=x-(1-3x)/4$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Multiply both sides by the common denominator 20.
steps: Thus −9=3x and x=−3.

problems.title: Two branches of an absolute value
problems.question: Solve $|2x/3-0.6|=|1/4-2/3|$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: The two roots are 61/40 and 11/40.

problems.title: A doubled median makes a parallelogram
problems.question: M is midpoint of AB and CM=MK on the median extension. ACM=28°,BCM=37°. Find CBK.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: If a quadrilateral’s diagonals bisect each other, it is a parallelogram.
steps: In ACBK, diagonals AB and CK bisect at M, so BK is parallel to AC. At C, angle ACB=28+37=65°.
The ray BK has the direction opposite CA. Therefore CBK is supplementary to ACB: 180−65=115°.

problems.title: A perpendicular bisector shortens a perimeter
problems.question: The perpendicular bisector of AB meets BC at M. BC=16 cm and perimeter AMC=26 cm. Find AC.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Points on the perpendicular bisector satisfy MA=MB.
steps: The perimeter AMC is MA+MC+AC=MB+MC+AC=BC+AC.
Thus AC=26−16=10 cm.

problems.title: Compare inverse-proportional pieces
problems.question: A 26 cm segment is divided inversely proportional to 2,3,4. What percentage of the largest piece is the smallest?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: The smallest-to-largest ratio is 3/6=1/2. Thus the smallest is 50% of the largest.

problems.title: Equilateral triangles outside a rectangle
problems.question: ABM and BCN are equilateral triangles built outside rectangle ABCD. Triangle MND has perimeter p. Find its side lengths and justify.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: Directly squaring DM,DN,MN gives the same value $w^2+h^2+\sqrt3wh$ for each.
Thus MND is equilateral. Its three equal sides total p, so each is p/3.

problems.title: A shared equation root determines a parameter
problems.question: For which c do $cx/7=x+c$ and $6-3(2x-4)=-8x+4$ have the same root?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Solve the parameter-free equation first, then substitute its root.
steps: 18−6x=−8x+4 gives x=−7. The first equation at −7 is −c=−7+c, so c=7/2.
At this c its x coefficient differs from 1, so it indeed has the unique root −7.

problems.title: Incenter and orthocenter angles
problems.question: O is the incenter and H the orthocenter of ABC. AOB is 14° greater than AHB. Find angle C.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: $\angle AOB=90^\circ+C/2$; if H is inside or opposite an obtuse C, $\angle AHB=180^\circ-C$.
steps: In this configuration, $90+C/2-(180-C)=14$. Thus 3C/2=104 and C=208/3 degrees.
If A or B were obtuse, the smaller angle AHB would instead equal C. Then 90−C/2=14 would force C=152°, incompatible with another obtuse angle.
So the valid triangle has C=69°20′; acute A,B with this C are possible.

problems.title: Counts from a weighted mean
problems.question: Between 40 and 50 nonzero numbers include positive and negative values. Overall mean is −3, positive mean 4, negative mean −8. Find the count.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: If P,N are the positive and negative counts, $4P-8N=-3(P+N)$.
steps: This gives 7P=5N, hence P=5k,N=7k and total=12k.
The only multiple of 12 strictly between 40 and 50 is 48, attained by P=20,N=28.
